title: Numbers 14:39–45
context: When Moses reports God’s words, the people mourn and then decide to go up and take the land after all. Moses warns that the LORD is not with them and that they will be defeated. They go up anyway without the ark or Moses, and the Amalekites and Canaanites drive them back to Hormah.

verses.text: Moses told these words to all the children of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
verses.arminianNotes: The people mourn greatly when they hear the sentence. Grief over consequences is not the same as trust in God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same distinction between sorrow over punishment and genuine repentance (compare 2 Corinthians 7:10). This is shared ground.

verses.text: They rose up early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Behold, we are here, and will go up to the place which the LORD has promised; for we have sinned.”
verses.arminianNotes: They rise early to go up, admitting “we have sinned.” But they now attempt what God has just forbidden. Their confession does not lead to obedience to God’s present word.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers also see a confession that falls short of submission. Both traditions see presumption replacing unbelief, which is still self-direction rather than faith.

verses.text: Moses said, “Why now do you disobey the commandment of the LORD, since it shall not prosper?
verses.arminianNotes: Moses asks why they now disobey, since it will not succeed. Obedience means following God’s word as it is given now, not as it was yesterday.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. The same act, going up, is faith on one day and rebellion the next, depending on God’s command. This is shared ground.

verses.text: Don’t go up, for the LORD isn’t among you; that way you won’t be struck down before your enemies.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses warns that the LORD is not among them. Without his presence, they will be struck down. The presence Joshua and Caleb had relied on (verse 9) is now withdrawn from this venture.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same point: success depends on God’s presence, not human resolve. This is shared ground.

verses.text: For there the Amalekite and the Canaanite are before you, and you will fall by the sword because you turned back from following the LORD; therefore the LORD will not be with you.”
verses.arminianNotes: Because they turned back from following the LORD, he will not be with them. The warning recalls their own words and choices.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers read this as the just consequence of rebellion. This is shared ground.

verses.text: But they presumed to go up to the top of the mountain. Nevertheless, the ark of the LORD’s covenant and Moses didn’t depart out of the camp.
verses.arminianNotes: They presume to go up anyway, but the ark of the covenant and Moses stay in the camp. Without the ark, the sign of God’s presence, the attempt is self-directed.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers also highlight the absence of the ark. Both traditions see presumption as trying to claim God’s promise on one’s own terms.

verses.text: Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites who lived in that mountain, and struck them and beat them down even to Hormah.
verses.arminianNotes: The Amalekites and Canaanites strike them down as far as Hormah. The defeat confirms Moses’ warning and ends the episode in tragedy.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. The chapter closes as a warning that both unbelief and presumption fail. This is shared ground.
